newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam coffee trade gears down for Tet holiday.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam coffee trade gears down for Tet holiday.

text.p: Vietnam's coffee market was quiet on Friday with trade slowing ahead of the traditional Tet Lunar New Year festival, dealers said.
The export price for Vietnamese robusta was quoted at about $1240-$1250 per tonne FOB Saigon Port midweek, with no new sales reported since then and farmers holding back on supplies.

"It's been a rough two weeks," said one trader. "At one stage last week the internal market collapsed by around $160. But then London prices started rising again, and since then everything's been quietening down ahead of Tet."
Dealers said there had been some delays in shipments because of congestion at Saigon Port earlier this week, but they dismissed rumours about possible defaults.

"I do know that some exporters have asked buyers if they can delay shipments. You can always argue that's a first sign of a default, but it hasn't led to defaults yet and I think they (the Vietnamese) are honestly trying to make sure they do perform," said one dealer.
"I've got one comment I'd like to make," said another. "No defaults."
Traders said they expected London prices to fall sharply by around $50 to $60 per tonne on Friday in response to the overnight tumble in New York.
"It depends if the speculators come in. If they decide to dump we could see a sharp drop before stabilising," one said.
Vietnam's Tet festival runs from February 6 through February 10. Trade is traditionally quiet a week on either side of this.
